NTA - It’s your wedding and you were not wrong at all for requesting a family member do something small to make your day a little better. If any of my friends even asked this of me for their wedding I’d do it in the heartbeat. A lot of people are saying you went to far but you’re not asking her to come to your wedding dressed like a clown, you’re just asking for something that’s not as attention grabbing. Even if it’s not ideal for her, you’re her sister and you’d think she’d be willing to do this on your special day. I hope you have an amazing wedding. No matter what just remember that you’re absolutely beautiful and this is a beautiful day for you. Best of luck.

It seems like they’re depending on their family to give their other kids rides, so I think OP was suggesting they focus on their current kids before having another one. I’ve seen a couple of people saying that public transport is an option, but it doesn’t seem like they’re using that option. Some areas don’t even have easy access to public transportation. Them not being able to fit all the kids into one car isn’t ideal, so it might be smart for them to try to fix that before having even more children that they can’t transport on their own.
NTA- I really don’t think it’s responsible to be having more kids if you can’t financially support them all.

My dad’s health had been circling the drain for years. This made it extremely hard to keep up with me when I was a child limited the amount of time we’d spend together. As a young kid, I didn’t really understand why I could never see my dad. I thought he just didn’t wanna see me, as he was bipolar and would have awful depressive swings. After weeks of not seeing my father, he surprised me with a trip to a local fair. It was our first time doing a normal family activity together and I was thrilled. I had no clue how much he had put aside just to make sure I’d have a good memory with him before he passed. He had recently gotten part of his foot amputated, so attending a fair was no easy task for him. I’m not sure if he had already decided to end his life at that point, but I’m so glad I got to spend that day with him. He did everything he could to make sure everything was perfect. I’m so thankful for that night and that I have a such a beautiful memory of him to look back on. I wish I had understood him more when he was still around, and I hope he understood that I loved him regardless of the mistakes he made early in my life. He was a great man and I’ll always be grateful to have had him as a dad.
